comments.author: @DeeAnna-u7q
comments.text:
I lived in the Philippines for fours years as a military dependent.  I came to love the country and her people.  It is breathtakingly beautiful and full of a rich history. 

One of my favorite buildings that I toured and fell in love with was the University of Santo Tomas built April 28, 1611.  While there I also saw Cirrigidor Island where prisinors of war were held in World War II.  One of my favorite city is Bagio - it reminded me of Colorado with pine trees, and the drive to Bagio was breath taking.  There is a huge lion's head carved into the side of the mountain.  Lower parts of elevation had verdent rice terraces.

I also loved going shopping in the markets, it offered more than you could imagine and then some.  The food was really good.  My family also attended many barrio celebrations, whole towns turned out for the celebration.  Every year the general population would re-enact the cruciation of Jesus Christ.  I only attended that once - at the invite of Remy, he worked for us as a gardener (which was referred to as a yard boy).

The Philippines has a rich history, and I am thankful to have had that experience - it made me aware of my own country and to appreciate and not take anything for granted.  It also taught me as well what abject poverty is like - and that also taught me to be more empathic and to help when I could.  Most of us do not realize how much we really have...I was humbled by the experience.  So thank you the people of the Philippines for sharing your country and the hearts of the Fillipino people along with your traditions - Salamat po!

replies.author: @DeeAnna-u7q
replies.text:
​@RaquelMartinez-r2xI was at Ckark AFB from 1978 to 1982.  I really miss it, I consider it my home away from home.  My little brother did have a dual citizenship, Buster (a family nickname) was born at Clark.  When he can to the United States he spoke Tagolog, Illicano, Pompangian, Visian and English. 

We hired a house girl named Ida, she and her small son whom was about a year older than my brother. Her husband was a fireman that lost his life in the line of duty.  I used to send her money every Christmas.  Once my family left after Mount Penotuba erupted, I lost contact, but I still think of her often. 

Thanks for responding, it was nice chatting with you.  I hear the weather in the Philippines has been rough.  I will keep you and your country in my prayers. Apologies if I did not correctly spell the words right.  😊❤😊
